extracted.intended_audience: data scientists, ML engineers, product managers, and AI/governance teams implementing model documentation in organizations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating, automating, and integrating Model Cards as standardized documentation for ML models to improve transparency, decision-making, and compliance. Focuses on the components to include, considerations for data/metrics/fairness, and options for automation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model documentation (code, data, model, training process)
rubrics_metrics.description: A thorough documentation of the ML development process consists of a code, data, and model documentation incl. the training process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model Cards provide a template/structure about what to add to your documentation. Automating the creation of Model Cards can improve both quality and speed of documentation and help ensure reproducibility, transparency and appropriate use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Details
rubrics_metrics.description: This section provides an overview of the model, including its name, version, and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May also include details about the model's architecture, parameters, and any pre-trained components used. It doesn’t need to contain sensitive information the organization doesn’t want to share, but rather convey basic information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Model Cards describe the intended use cases and applications of the model, specifying the tasks it is designed to perform and the target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quickly convey why, for whom and for what purpose the model was created so stakeholders can assess suitability for deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary of model performance across a variety of relevant factors including groups, instrumentation, and environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include groups (e.g. people of the same gender), instrumentation (e.g. which camera was used for input pictures), and environments (e.g. lighting conditions). These external factors are included to point to potential limitations of the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: List of performance metrics and decision thresholds used to evaluate the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that suitable metrics vary with the type of model tested; choose metrics appropriate to the task and include thresholds and how metrics were computed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information about the source and composition for all referenced datasets used for validation and testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document provenance, splits, sampling, and any known limitations of evaluation datasets so results can be interpreted and reproduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about the training data used to build the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally follows the same level of transparency as evaluation data, but often unfeasible due to privacy restraints. For external communication, basic details about distributions over groups in the data and potential biases should suffice; note privacy constraints where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of evaluating the model according to the chosen metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present quantitative results broken down by relevant factors (e.g., group-level performance, environment conditions) to surface differential behavior and support informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of potential bias, fairness, and ethical considerations related to the model and its deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address issues such as algorithmic bias, fairness in prediction outcomes, potential societal impacts, and steps taken (or not taken) to mitigate concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats & Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional concerns not covered in the previous sections including limitations and risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section for awareness information when using the model, limitations, dependencies, trade-offs, and explicit recommendations for safe or appropriate use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Model Cards should be clear and concise so stakeholders can understand the model's behavior and make informed decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write documentation targeted to its audience, avoiding overly technical detail where unnecessary; emphasize key facts that affect deployment and risk assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automation and standardization of Model Cards
rubrics_metrics.description: Automating creation of Model Cards reduces manual documentation time and helps standardize information across models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automation can decrease documentation time (example: Wayflyer reported a ~10x reduction) and ensure model, data and meta information are standardized and easy to digest. Consider tools (open-source toolkits, internal tooling, or plug & play solutions) compatible with your stack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-specific abstraction levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide different abstraction levels of documentation so non-technical stakeholders can understand model use cases, implications and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare simplified summaries for business, legal or policy stakeholders while retaining detailed technical appendices for engineers and auditors; leveraging AI or templating can help generate multiple abstraction levels.
